claims.text: Conventional cast AlCoCrFeNi has a coarse, heterogeneous precipitate distribution.
Conventional cast AlCoCrFeNi forms a discontinuous or nonprotective oxide scale.
An addition of approximately 0.5 at.% Hf can help tailor the precipitate morphology of an AlCoCrFeNi-based alloy.
Directional solidification or controlled grain refinement can produce a fine, coherent gamma-prime precipitate distribution.
Multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi alloys can contain coherent nanoscale precipitates.
A refined coherent gamma-prime precipitate distribution increases mechanical strength through precipitation hardening.
Refining the precipitate microstructure promotes formation of a dense, continuous, self-healing aluminum-rich oxide layer.
A continuous aluminum-rich oxide layer inhibits continued oxidation.
A continuous aluminum-rich oxide layer improves corrosion resistance in chloride-containing environments.
Precipitation strengthening and oxide-scale protection act synergistically in the proposed alloy.
The proposed modification imposes no significant density penalty because aluminum is intrinsically light.
The modified, directionally solidified alloy will have higher tensile strength than a conventionally cast baseline.
The modified, directionally solidified alloy will have more reproducible tensile strength than a conventionally cast baseline.
The modified alloy will exhibit reduced oxidation weight gain and a lower parabolic oxidation-rate constant.
The modified alloy will exhibit improved corrosion resistance relative to the baseline.
The protective oxide scale may become unstable at temperatures significantly above 900 degrees Celsius.
High chloride concentrations may cause the proposed performance advantage to cease.
Formation of unintended deleterious phases may compromise mechanical integrity or corrosion resistance.

contradictions.description: The causal hypothesis requires the targeted precipitates and oxide scale to be present and then produce improved performance, but the stated falsification rule requires both absent performance improvements and absence of the targeted microstructure. Failure to create the mediator tests implementation rather than falsifying the claimed mediator-to-performance mechanism; conversely, observing the mediator without improved performance would directly challenge the mechanism but would not satisfy the stated rule.
